short: A 30-metre marble column spiralled with relief carvings narrating Trajan's two wars in Dacia.
full:
Trajan's Column was dedicated on 12 May 113 CE in the forum built from the proceeds of his Dacian campaigns of 101–102 and 105–106. A continuous helical frieze, some 190 metres long if unwound, winds around the shaft in low relief, showing more than 2,500 figures across scenes of river crossings, fort-building, sieges and battle, culminating in the suicide of the Dacian king Decebalus. An internal spiral staircase of 185 steps climbs to a viewing platform that once carried a bronze statue of Trajan, replaced in 1587 by one of Saint Peter.

An inscription at the base records that the column's height marked the depth of earth removed to level the site for the forum, though modern measurement makes the claim only roughly accurate. After Trajan's death in 117 his ashes were interred in the column's base, an honour unique among Roman emperors. The frieze survives as the single most detailed visual record of the Roman army in the field, still used by historians to study equipment and tactics of the period.
